page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.32-128 is an ARM-based compute instance powered by Ampere AmpereOne-M processors. The configuration features 64 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 3.6 GHz, assigning 64 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core to eliminate noisy-neighbor thread contention. System memory is sized at 128.0 GB, providing an allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per dedicated core.

The instance operates without integrated local NVMe storage and includes no discrete graphics hardware. Persistent disk operations must rely on external cloud block volumes. One complimentary public IPv4 address is assigned to the instance for direct network reachability.

With its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio and dedicated single-threaded architecture, the instance provides high compute density for multi-threaded arm64 applications. It is appropriate for parallel software compilation, high-concurrency microservices, continuous integration pipelines, batch data transforms, and multi-core tasks with moderate per-thread memory demands.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.A4.Flex.32-128 is an arm64 compute-oriented virtual machine built on Ampere AmpereOne-M hardware. It delivers 64 dedicated physical cores running at 3.6 GHz with one thread per core, translating directly to 64 dedicated vCPUs without hyperthreading overhead. The system is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes no onboard GPU accelerators and features no local drive storage, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent data. Network routing is enabled by one complimentary public IPv4 address. Given its dedicated single-thread core topology and dense execution layout, this shape delivers efficient compute performance for parallel ARM software builds, microservices architectures, continuous integration runners, containerized web clusters, and multi-core batch processing operations.
